general election.note: No single standard term. For national parliaments use 'Parlamentswahl' or 'Bundestagswahl'/'Nationalratswahl'. For the US, 'allgemeine Wahl' or 'Hauptwahl' (as opposed to 'Vorwahl'). UK: 'Unterhauswahl'.

primary.note: Press also uses 'Primary' (pl. 'Primaries'); 'Vorwahl' is the established German term. Not to be confused with a telephone area code.

runoff.note: Used in Germany, Austria and Switzerland (e.g. Bundespräsidentenwahl in Austria; cantonal executive elections in Switzerland).

first round.note: Swiss usage: 'erster Wahlgang'. Also 'erste Runde' in press for foreign elections.

by-election.note: UK 'by-election' often rendered 'Nachwahl' or 'Nachwahl zum Unterhaus'. Swiss: 'Ersatzwahl' (for filling a vacancy). Germany: 'Nachwahl' or 'Ersatzwahl'.

special election.note: Also 'außerplanmäßige Wahl' or 'Nachwahl' where it fills a vacancy. 'Sonderwahl' is the common rendering for US usage.

recall election.note: Also 'Abwahl' (removal). For Switzerland 'Abberufung'. US: 'Recall-Wahl' is common in press. Germany has 'Abwahl' of mayors via 'Bürgerentscheid'.

contest.note: Pl. 'Rennen'. Never 'Wahlkampf', which means a campaign. Use 'Wahl' with the office named when it reads better (e.g. 'Senatswahl in Texas').

race.note: Informal, as in 'Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen'. In tables use 'Wahl' with the office named.

ballot measure.note: Swiss usage 'Abstimmungsvorlage' / 'Vorlage'. For US ballot measures, press says 'Volksabstimmung' or 'Abstimmung über ...'. Generic: 'Sachfrage' or 'Sachabstimmung'.

referendum.note: Pl. 'Referenden' (also 'Referenda'). Germany: 'Volksentscheid' for binding votes; Switzerland: 'Referendum' (optional/mandatory) and 'Volksabstimmung'; Austria: 'Volksabstimmung'.

initiative.note: Swiss: 'Volksinitiative'. Germany: 'Volksbegehren' (petition stage) leading to 'Volksentscheid'; Austria: 'Volksbegehren'.

proposition.note: US usage: 'Proposition 8' etc.; rendered as 'Proposition' (pl. 'Propositionen') in press, sometimes explained as 'Abstimmungsvorlage'.

retention election.note: For US judges: 'Bestätigungswahl für Richter'. Press often explains: 'Wahl über den Verbleib im Amt'.

candidate.note: Feminine 'Kandidatin'; plural 'Kandidaten'. Official language also 'Bewerber' (Bundeswahlgesetz uses 'Bewerber'). Gender-neutral 'Kandidierende' is used in Switzerland.

incumbent.note: Feminine 'Amtsinhaberin'. Also 'Titelverteidiger' informally; for MPs 'bisheriger Abgeordneter'. Swiss: 'bisher' (e.g. 'Bisherige').

nominee.note: Feminine 'nominierte Kandidatin'. US: 'Kandidat der Partei' / 'Präsidentschaftskandidat'. Official: 'aufgestellter Bewerber'.

write-in.note: US concept; no equivalent in German law. Press: 'Write-in-Stimme'. Abbreviated 'Write-in'.

unopposed.note: Phrase: 'ohne Gegenkandidaten gewählt'. Swiss: 'in stiller Wahl gewählt' (tacit election when candidates equal seats), also 'stille Wahl'.

votes cast.note: Plural only; in the nominative: 'die abgegebenen Stimmen'. Inflects as adjective.

blank votes.note: Swiss: 'leere Stimmen' / 'leere Stimmzettel'. In Germany blank ballots count as invalid; in Switzerland they are counted separately.

registered voters.note: Plural; adjectival noun ('die Wahlberechtigten'). Swiss: 'Stimmberechtigte'. Also 'eingetragene Wähler' for US registration.

electorate.note: Also 'Wahlvolk'; 'Wahlberechtigte' for those entitled to vote. Swiss: 'Stimmberechtigte'.

vote share.note: Also 'Stimmanteil'; Swiss: 'Wähleranteil' for parties. Press: 'Prozent der Stimmen'.

swing.note: Press also uses 'Stimmenverschiebung' or 'Verschiebung der Stimmenanteile'; Swiss: 'Wählerverschiebung'.

majority.note: 'absolute Mehrheit' for more than half; 'einfache Mehrheit' for plurality.

plurality.note: Also 'einfache Mehrheit'. Swiss: 'relatives Mehr' ('absolutes Mehr' for majority).

seat.note: Pl. 'Sitze'. Also 'Mandat' (pl. 'Mandate'), the official term in electoral law.

constituency.note: Pl. 'Wahlkreise'. Used for UK constituencies and for Germany's Wahlkreise.

electoral district.note: Also 'Wahlbezirk' (in Germany a smaller unit for polling, 'Stimmbezirk'). Swiss: 'Wahlkreis'.

district.note: US: 'Kongresswahlbezirk' / 'Wahlbezirk' ('Kongressdistrikt' in press). Swiss 'Bezirk' is an administrative unit.

ward.note: UK ward: 'Ward' also appears in press. Alternative: 'Stadtbezirk' or 'Stadtteil'.

precinct.note: US precinct, in press 'Wahlbezirk' or 'Stimmbezirk'. In Germany 'Stimmbezirk' is the smallest unit (Urnenwahlbezirk).

reporting unit.note: Coined term, no standard equivalent. Official: 'Auszählungsbezirk' or 'Gebietseinheit'.

county.note: US: 'County' (pl. 'Countys' or 'Counties'), established in press. UK: 'Grafschaft' (pl. 'Grafschaften'). Germany's 'Landkreis' is not an equivalent.

province.note: Pl. 'Provinzen'. Turkish 'il': 'Provinz'. Swiss/Austria: not used for subnational units.

polity.note: No exact equivalent. For countries or territories use 'Staat oder Gebiet', 'Land' or 'Hoheitsgebiet'.

chamber.note: Pl. 'Kammern'. Also 'Haus' for US House; Swiss: 'Rat' (Nationalrat, Ständerat).

legislature.note: Also 'gesetzgebende Körperschaft' or 'Parlament'. US state: 'Parlament' or 'Legislative'.

lower house.note: Pl. 'Unterhäuser'. Also 'Erste Kammer' or 'Volkskammer' in other contexts. UK: 'Unterhaus'.

upper house.note: Also 'Zweite Kammer'. Germany's Bundesrat, Swiss Ständerat as examples.

mayor.note: Feminine 'Bürgermeisterin'. Large cities: 'Oberbürgermeister'. Swiss: 'Stadtpräsident' / 'Gemeindepräsident'. Berlin, Hamburg: 'Regierender Bürgermeister' / 'Erster Bürgermeister'.

governor.note: Feminine 'Gouverneurin'. Pl. 'Gouverneure'. Swiss: 'Regierungsrat' for cantonal executives.

independent.note: Feminine 'Parteilose'; adjectival noun. Also 'unabhängiger Kandidat'; Germany: 'Einzelbewerber' in electoral law.

closed list.note: Also 'geschlossene Liste'. 'Starre Liste' is the established term in Germany's electoral law debates.

open list.note: Also 'flexible Liste'. Swiss: 'Panaschieren' and 'Kumulieren' are specific vote options.

preference vote.note: Austria: 'Vorzugsstimme'. Swiss: 'Kumulieren' (giving two votes). Germany (state elections): 'Personenstimme'.

constituency seat.note: Pl. 'Direktmandate'. Official German term for directly elected seats.

overhang seat.note: Pl. 'Überhangmandate'. Abolished effect at federal level since 2023 reform (no overhang seats awarded).

first past the post.note: More exact: 'relative Mehrheitswahl'. British system: 'Mehrheitswahlrecht'. Also 'First-past-the-post' in press.

single transferable vote.note: Also 'Single Transferable Vote' / 'STV' in press. Official German: 'Einzelstimmübertragung'.

mixed-member proportional.note: Germany's official description of its system. Generic: 'Grabensystem' is mixed non-compensatory (parallel).

D'Hondt method.note: Also 'Divisorverfahren mit Abrundung'. Used in Austria and Switzerland ('Proporz nach D'Hondt').

Sainte-Laguë method.note: Also 'Sainte-Laguë/Schepers' in Germany (current federal method), 'Divisorverfahren mit Standardrundung'.

elimination.note: Noun: 'Ausscheiden des Kandidaten'; or 'Eliminierung'. Rare outside STV.

official results.note: Germany: 'amtliches Endergebnis' (declared by Bundeswahlleiter). Pl. 'amtliche Endergebnisse'. Also 'amtliches Ergebnis'.

called.note: As status: 'Sieger ausgerufen' / 'Wahlsieg verkündet'. Press: 'zum Sieger erklärt'.

projection.note: Hochrechnung is the standard projection based on counted votes; 'Prognose' is the exit-poll forecast at poll closing.

too close to call.note: Press: 'Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen', 'noch offen'. Not a fixed term.

reporting.note: Also 'ausgezählte Stimmbezirke'. Percent counted: 'Anteil der ausgezählten Wahlbezirke'.

absentee ballot.note: In Germany 'Briefwahl' covers postal and absentee voting. Swiss: 'briefliche Stimmabgabe'. Austria: 'Wahlkarte'.

mail-in ballot.note: The vote itself: 'Briefwahl'. Individual: 'Briefwahlstimme'. Swiss: 'briefliche Stimmabgabe'.

early voting.note: Austria: 'vorgezogene Stimmabgabe'; Swiss: 'vorzeitige Stimmabgabe'. Press for US: 'Early Voting'.

flip.note: Press: 'Sitzwechsel' or 'Wechsel der Partei'. Verb: 'kippen' ('der Sitz kippt').

gerrymander.note: Neuter noun, used as in English ('das Gerrymandering'). Also 'manipulativer Zuschnitt von Wahlkreisen'.

convention.note: US: 'Nominierungsparteitag' or 'Convention' in press ('Nominierungsparteitag der Demokraten').

roll call.note: For US conventions: 'Delegiertenabstimmung nach Bundesstaaten'. Press: 'Roll Call'.

turnover.note: Also 'Wechsel' or 'Fluktuation' (e.g. 'Fluktuation im Parlament'). No standard term.

changeset.note: Technical term; 'Changeset' is often retained in software contexts.

coverage.note: Also 'Erfassungsgrad' or 'Umfang'. Media coverage would be 'Berichterstattung'.

shapes.note: Also 'Gebietsgrenzen' or 'Shapes' in GIS contexts. Singular 'Geometrie'.

bounty.note: Coined; alternatives 'Kopfgeld' (unsuitable) or 'Bounty'. Describe as 'Aufgabe mit Prämie'.
